name: MDM hub
description: A master data management hub resolves the same real-world entity — customer, product, supplier — scattered inconsistently across CRMs, ERPs, and product databases into one golden record. Source records flow in, an ML-assisted match/merge engine clusters records that refer to the same entity, survivorship rules pick winning attribute values, human stewards adjudicate the uncertain middle through a review UI, and golden records publish back out via API and warehouse tables. The stewardship loop is not optional garnish: match models produce a gray zone by construction, and the hubs that work are the ones where humans efficiently clear it and their decisions retrain the matcher.
when_to_use: Choose this when the same entities live in multiple systems and the inconsistency has a business cost you can name — duplicate customer outreach, compliance reports that disagree, M&A integrations, a 360-degree customer view that is actually six different views.
It presupposes executive sponsorship for cross-system data ownership, because match/merge is the easy half; agreeing whose attribute wins is the hard half.
The same customer exists in five systems and nobody agrees which record is right.
when_not_to_use: Skip the hub if entities effectively live in one system — enforce quality at the source instead.
Deduplication within a single analytical table is the entity-resolution archetype without hub machinery: run the matcher in the pipeline and move on.
And do not start MDM as a technology project without governance mandate; a hub nobody stewards and no system trusts is the most expensive way to produce another conflicting copy.

hot_spots.title: Match thresholds
hot_spots.detail: Too-loose matching merges different people; too-strict spawns duplicates.

hot_spots.title: Steward backlog
hot_spots.detail: Ambiguous matches pile up and golden records go stale.

hot_spots.title: Survivorship rules
hot_spots.detail: Wrong precedence lets a stale system overwrite fresh truth.

stages.name: Sources
stages.role: Feed candidate records from CRMs, ERPs, and operational databases into the hub with source lineage preserved
stages.rationale: Getting records into the hub is ordinary EL — Airbyte/Fivetran connectors for the SaaS and database sources, dlt for the odd ones, Debezium when golden records must track source changes in near real time. The MDM-specific requirement is lineage: every candidate record must carry its source system and source key immutably, because survivorship rules and steward decisions are expressed in terms of which system said what. Standardize and cleanse (casing, addresses, phone formats) on the way in — matching quality is mostly preprocessing quality.

stages.name: Landing
stages.role: Raw landing of source entity extracts before standardization and matching
stages.rationale: Cheap immutable object storage as the landing layer decouples ingestion from processing: replays, backfills, and audits read the raw dump instead of re-extracting from sources.

stages.name: Match/merge
stages.role: Cluster records referring to the same entity and compute golden records via survivorship rules
stages.rationale: Zingg is the open-source, Spark-based matcher: active-learning training on your own data, blocking to keep pairwise comparison tractable at scale, and output that lands as tables in the stack you already run — the right starting point for a data-team-led hub. Senzing is a purpose-built entity-resolution engine with excellent out-of-the-box accuracy on person/company data and real-time resolution APIs, the pick when you would rather configure than train; Tamr brings ML-driven mastering with enterprise handholding; Informatica MDM is the full-suite incumbent when the org wants matching, workflow, and governance in one (expensive) box. Keep survivorship rules explicit and versioned regardless of engine — 'most recent non-null from the most trusted source' style rules are business policy, not tuning parameters.

stages.name: Steward UI
stages.role: Human review of uncertain matches and merge decisions — a workflow surface with no dedicated corpus entry; build thin or use a suite's built-in console
stages.rationale: No standalone corpus tool owns this seat. The build path is a thin internal app (Streamlit is the fastest credible version) presenting match pairs in the confidence gray zone with approve/reject/split actions, writing decisions back as matcher training data and survivorship overrides. The buy path is the consoles inside MDM suites (Informatica, Reltio), which add workflow, audit, and role management you would otherwise rebuild. Two design rules either way: stewards see source lineage and confidence for every pair, and every decision is captured as labeled data — a stewardship queue that does not retrain the matcher is a treadmill.

stages.name: Publish
stages.role: Expose golden records: a lookup/API surface for operational consumers and tables for analytics
stages.rationale: Publishing is dual-channel by nature. Operationally, golden records and the crosswalk (source key to master key) live in a database backing a thin API — Postgres is the boring, right answer, with Redis caching in front if lookup volume demands it. Analytically, the same tables land in the warehouse so every mart joins through master keys instead of per-source identities — which is where most of the ROI quietly materializes. Hightouch closes the loop by syncing golden attributes back into the CRMs that fed the hub, turning MDM from a reporting fix into source-system hygiene.
